    Trading words, explained simply
    Buy / Long
    A trade that aims to gain if the price rises. It loses if the price falls, and trading costs also affect the result.
    Sell / Short
    A trade that aims to gain if the price falls. It loses if the price rises, and trading costs also affect the result.
    Entry
    The price where a trade starts. A possible entry is not an instruction to trade now.
    Stop
    An order intended to exit when a trade moves against you. Fast price changes can make the loss larger than expected.
    Target
    A price where you might plan to exit. The market may never reach it.
    Leverage
    Taking a larger position with less money set aside. It can increase losses and lead to liquidation, where the exchange closes the position.
    USDT
    A crypto token designed to track the US dollar. SOLUSDT shows the price of SOL in USDT. USDT is not a bank deposit and can lose value.
    Signal
    A result from the app’s checks, not a guarantee about what the price will do next.

    How the analysis works

    Every assessment follows the same trend, confirmation, and risk checks.

    Direction first

    EMA 20 and EMA 50 on the higher timeframe must agree with price and slope.

    Confirm the move

    A completed candle must clear the previous 20-candle range, with RSI confirmation and at least 1.2× average volume.

    Account for risk

    Stops use 1.2× ATR. Targets project 1.5× and 2.5× price risk. Net reward/risk must reach 1.5×, with no nearby opposing pivot.

    Data, limitations, and signal rules

    Market source: Binance USDⓈ-M public futures REST and WebSocket feeds. Live mark prices are requested every second; actual delivery depends on the exchange and connection. Completed-candle analysis refreshes every 60 seconds and after a candle closes. Signals are suppressed after 10 seconds without a fresh quote or 90 seconds without a fresh analysis.

    Monitoring works while this page is open and visible. It pauses when hidden and refreshes before resuming. Reconnection uses bounded exponential backoff; requests respect exchange rate-limit cooldowns. There is no background server or promise of alerts after closing the app.

    Holding-time mappings: 15 minutes → 1m entry / 15m trend; 1 hour → 5m entry / 1h trend; 4 hours → 15m entry / 4h trend; 1 day → 1h entry / 1d trend. The horizon selects analysis intervals, not a promised time to reach a target.

    Long RSI must be 55–75; short RSI must be 25–45. A move more than 0.8 ATR beyond its trigger is extended. Opposing swing pivots within 1.5× price risk block a signal. A live price that loses the breakout, crosses the stop, reaches target 1, or extends too far removes the entry signal.

    This is an unvalidated technical heuristic, not a trained prediction model. No backtested win rate is claimed. It does not analyze news, order-book depth, or your portfolio. Futures can liquidate collateral, and stop fills can slip. No orders are placed and no exchange credentials are requested. Calculator balances stay in this browser and are not saved.
